references.text: The sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who also came, for there was famine in the land of Canaan.
When the famine spread over all the land, Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
There was no food in all the land, for the famine was very severe, so the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan were exhausted by the famine.
A famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great distress, and our fathers found no food.
The verses show the theological and economic escalation from selling grain to total loss of land ownership due to the severity of the famine.
The candidate highlights the direct causal link between the global famine and Joseph's brothers as the first to come to buy grain.
The candidate illuminates the economic process (money collection) that was necessary to sustain the grain trade described in the source verse.
The candidate explains the existential motivation (life or death) behind the people's arrival in Egypt to buy grain.
The verses compare Joseph's global role as a food provider with his specific authority over his brothers in the same context.
The candidate provides a concrete detail about the sales process (grain and money) that expands on the general trade described in the source verse.
